novel_mechanics_found: L4 hunter evasion is an axis-speed race: a highest-tier fruit can outrun a 7-colored hunter with repeated 8-pixel axial hops, allowing a decoy f to be parked at the far edge while the other half is built. L5 introduces two hunters; making them converge fuses them into an e-colored composite thief. The composite follows the active fruit and repeatedly degrades it, but L5 supplies exactly enough surplus mass to survive those losses. L6 introduces high tiers c and 8 plus a hunter-processing/socket interaction: an 8 can be downgraded to c and then to the required b through timed collision/withdrawal, with the level transition resolving one tick later. L7 is a synchronized race: four 6 fruits form one b in four actions while the hunter converts 8 to c to b; both b fruits can then be delivered before the next attack. L8 scouting found three hunters, two c goals, four blobs, and an e goal; two hunters fuse on tick 6, while careless clicks within radius of both c fruits merge them back into an 8.
narrative: Replayed and confirmed the 39-action banked prefix to Level 3, then solved Levels 4 through 7 by rendered-frame experimentation. Level 4 required kiting the hunter with a far-edge f decoy; Level 5 required hunter fusion plus exact mass accounting; Level 6 exposed a timed high-tier downgrade/socket mechanic; and Level 7 compressed construction and delivery into an eight-action race. A fresh reproduction gate replayed the full 132-action sequence and reached Level 7. I then investigated Level 8 but stopped at a genuine simultaneous-control wall: keeping both c fruits separated and safe while preserving the fused e and avoiding the third hunter remained unresolved.
gotchas: The Level 4 hunter advances about four pixels per axis toward the active/highest fruit; long axis-aligned 8-pixel fruit hops create separation, while diagonal hops often do not.
A hunter collision may be rendered as partial occlusion for one frame; the fruit can survive if moved continuously, but an unmoved fruit is downgraded on the following action.
Two 7-colored hunters can collide and fuse into an e-colored composite thief. The e sprite can remain largely hidden under a fruit and then repeatedly downgrade it on later actions.
In Level 5 the resource meter is nearly exact: the verified line reaches the final target with only the last few meter cells remaining; avoid extra failed clicks.
Level 6 collision resolution can be deferred: the verified tail reaches the win after a far failed click following the final c/hunter positioning.
Level 7 needs two hops for the right b, via (48,24) then (44,22); clicking (44,22) directly from its spawn is outside pull range and wastes the critical timing window.
Level 8: after the two b fruits merge into one c and the 8 is downgraded into the other c, never click a point within pull radius of both c fruits or they merge back into an 8.
env.reset() restarts the current level without replaying earlier levels; only a fresh environment should receive the full banked prefix.
